sourcedFrom: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The APC9 PRO comes apart on TWO TAKE-DOWN PINS pushed left to right, and then in an order most AR-shaped guns do not use: stock out of the upper receiver FIRST, then the recoil spring out the back, then a BOLT SECURING PIN sideways, then the bolt. ⛔ Two rules bracket the whole job — the telescopic stock must be EXTENDED before the rear take-down pin will push out, and B&T says do not operate the trigger while the weapon is disassembled.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE, magazine out, chamber LOOKED AT, bolt locked open
steps.action: Rotate the fire selector to the «safe» position — B&T marks the positions on BOTH sides of the weapon, WHITE DOT = SAFE. Press the magazine retainer and pull the magazine downward out. Pull the charging handle fully to the rear and inspect the chamber VISUALLY. Then lock the bolt open.
steps.prose: Four actions, in B&T's order, and the bolt ends up held open so the chamber stays visible while you work.
steps.quote: c.	 Pull the charging handle completely to the rear and in­spect the chamber visually to be clear.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 4.1 Clearing weapon, step c, p.25

steps.title: ⛔ Both take-down pins LEFT TO RIGHT — the lower comes loose
steps.action: With the weapon clear and the bolt CLOSED, press the front and rear take-down pin from the LEFT side to the RIGHT side and pull them out from the right until the lower receiver comes loose. Then separate the lower receiver from the weapon.
steps.prose: Direction matters on captured pins — from the left, out to the right, every time.
steps.quote:
c.	 Press the front and rear take-down pin from left side to 
right side and pull it out from right side until the lower re­ceiver comes loose.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5. Maintenance procedures, step c, p.39

steps.title: ⚠ The telescopic stock must be EXTENDED to push the rear pin out
steps.action: If the rear take-down pin will not move, this is why: B&T states the telescopic stock must be in the EXTRACTED position for pushing out the rear take-down pin. Extend it first, then push.
steps.prose: A collapsed stock physically blocks the pin's path. It is not a stiff pin, it is a blocked one.
steps.quote: The telescopic stock must be in extracted posi­tion for pushing out the rear take-down pin.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.1 Disassembly of the weapon — Advice, p.40
steps.warn:
DO NOT OPERATE THE TRIGGER WHEN THE 
WEAPON IS DISASSEMBLED.

steps.title: Stock DOWN and back out of the upper receiver
steps.action: Grasp the stock, press it DOWN, and pull it back out of the upper receiver. Down first — it is a two-motion release, and pulling straight back without pressing down fights the catch.
steps.prose: On this weapon the stock comes off before anything internal moves, which is the opposite of an AR.
steps.quote:
e.	 Grasp the stock, press it down and pull it back out of the 
upper receiver.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.1 Disassembly of the weapon, step e, p.40

steps.title: Recoil spring out the BACK, on the charging handle
steps.action: Pull the charging handle backwards until the recoil spring can be grasped, then pull the recoil spring backwards out of the lower receiver.
steps.prose: The charging handle is what gives you access — the spring is not reachable with the bolt forward.
steps.quote:
f.	 Pull the charging handle backwards until the recoil spring 
can be grasped, then pull the recoil spring backwards 
out of the lower receiver.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.1 Disassembly of the weapon, step f, p.41

steps.title: ⚠ BOLT SECURING PIN — line it up with the cutout, then sideways out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle FURTHER back until the bolt securing pin is congruent with the cutout in the upper receiver. Then pull the lock pin out SIDEWAYS and remove it. Only then does the bolt pull rearward out of the receiver.
steps.prose: It is an alignment gate, like a witness mark: the pin only clears at one position of the bolt.
steps.aside: h.	 Pull the bolt rearward out of the receiver and remove it.
steps.quote:
g.	 Pull the charging handle further back until the bolt secur­ing pin is congruent with the cutout in the upper receiver. 
Pull out the lock pin sideways and remove it from the 
upper receiver.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.1 Disassembly of the weapon, step g, p.41

steps.title: ⚠ Your STOCK may have its own manual — B&T says so
steps.action: Two steps above depend on the stock: the telescopic stock must be EXTENDED before the rear take-down pin will move, and it goes back in and UP on reassembly. ⛔ If your weapon carries an M4 stock on the stock adapter rather than a B&T stock, this book does not cover how that stock operates — B&T sends you to the operating manual of the respective stock.
steps.prose: A separate manual for a part that gates the strip is worth knowing about before you are holding a pin punch.
steps.quote: The operation of an M4 stock mounted on the stock adapter can be found in the operating manual of the respective stock.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — Stocks / Adapters, p.34

steps.title: Barrel from the REAR — copper brush, suitable-length rod
steps.action: Use a cleaning rod of suitable length with a COPPER brush and clean the barrel FROM THE REAR SIDE. Rear entry protects the muzzle, and a rod that is too short will not carry the brush clear at the far end.
steps.prose: Breech-end entry is the same discipline every serious maker prints, for the same reason: the crown.
steps.quote:
a.	 Use a cleaning rod of suitable length with a copper brush 
to clean the barrel from the rear side.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.2 Cleaning and inspections, step a, p.43

steps.title: Small brush into the CAVITIES of both receivers, then an oiled rag
steps.action: Use a small brush to remove particles captured in the cavities of the lower AND upper receiver — on a blowback PCC that is where the fouling actually collects. Then wipe all accessible surfaces clean with an oiled rag.
steps.prose: "Cavities" is the word that matters. The flat surfaces look clean long before the corners are.
steps.quote:
b.	 Use a small brush to remove particles captured in the 
cavities of lower and upper receiver.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.2 Cleaning and inspections, step b, p.43

steps.title: INSPECT for cracks and deformation — then a slight oil film on the steel
steps.action: Inspect all components and accessible parts for cracks, deformations or other signs of deterioration. Then apply a SLIGHT film of oil to all accessible surfaces of STEEL parts. ⛔ If the serviceability of the weapon seems doubtful, B&T's instruction is to go to an armorer.
steps.prose: Inspection is a numbered step in this book, not advice at the end of one.
steps.quote:
d.	 Inspect all components and accessible parts for cracks, 
deformations or other signs of deterioration.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.2 Cleaning and inspections, step d, p.43
steps.warn: ADDRESS TO AN ARMORER IF THE SERVICE­ABILITY OF THE WEAPON SEEMS DOUBTFUL.

steps.title: ⚠ Recoil spring goes in CURVED END FIRST
steps.action: Bolt into the upper receiver, pushed in until it aligns with the cutout for the bolt securing pin — which B&T says may be inserted from EITHER side, as the user prefers. Then the recoil spring into the housing. ⛔ Check its alignment: it goes into the lock CURVED END FIRST.
steps.prose: A spring in backwards will assemble and will not run. That is why B&T boxes this one as an Advice.
steps.quote:
Check the alignment of the recoil spring! Insert 
the recoil spring into the lock with the curved end 
first.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.3.1 Reassembly of the weapon — Advice, p.44

steps.title: Stock in and UP, lower on, pins from the RIGHT
steps.action: Insert the stock into the receiver and push it UPWARDS. Place the lower receiver on the upper and push the front and rear take-down pins in from the RIGHT side — the opposite direction from removal. ⚠ The telescopic stock must be extended for this too.
steps.prose: Out to the right, back in from the right. The pins have a head and a detent end and they only go one way.
steps.quote:
g.	 Place the lower receiver on the upper receiver and push 
in the front and rear take-down pin from the right side.
steps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.3.1 Reassembly of the weapon, step g, p.44

deepSteps.title: Upper receiver — BOTH charging handles out sideways
deepSteps.action: Pull the charging handle back until it is congruent with the cutout in the receiver, then pull BOTH charging handles out sideways and remove them from the handguard. Push the charging handle carrier out of the FRONT of the upper receiver using the cleaning rod.
deepSteps.prose: Two handles, one carrier. The cleaning rod is the tool B&T names for pushing the carrier out, and it is already in your kit.
deepSteps.quote:
b.	 Pull out booth charging handles sideways and remove it 
from the handguard.
deepSteps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.2 Disassembly upper receiver, step b, p.42

deepSteps.title: ⚠ With a suppressor fitted the order changes — can, safety pin, handguard
deepSteps.action: If the weapon carries a suppressor, B&T publishes a different upper-receiver strip: unscrew the suppressor, loosen and remove the SAFETY PIN, then pull the hand guard FORWARD away from the housing and remove it, and only then go to the charging handles.
deepSteps.prose: Three extra steps in a fixed order, and the safety pin is the one that is easy to miss and impossible to work around.
deepSteps.quote: b.	 Loosen and remove the safety pin.
deepSteps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 5.1.3 Disassembly upper receiver with suppressor, step b, p.42

deepSteps.title: ⚠ B&T's own service interval — and the ammunition rule that voids the guarantee
deepSteps.action: B&T asks that the weapon be presented to the unit armorer for inspection after each mission, or at minimum once per year. ⛔ And the guarantee has a hard edge: defects traceable to non-NATO, non-SAAMI or non-CIP ammunition — reloaded cartridges especially — are not covered.
deepSteps.prose: An annual floor rather than a round count, which suits a weapon that may sit more than it shoots.
deepSteps.quote:
3.	 The weapon is to be presented to the unit armorer for inspection after each mission or a minimum 
of once per year.
deepSteps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 1.2 Maintenance rules, rule 3, p.17
deepSteps.warn: Defects that can be traced back to the use of non NATO, SAAMI or CIP ammunition (espe­cially reloaded cartridges) are not covered by the guarantee!

deepSteps.title: A misfire waits THIRTY SECONDS before the chamber opens
deepSteps.action: If a cartridge fails to ignite, keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction and open the chamber only after a MINIMUM of 30 seconds. A hang fire that goes off with the chamber opening is the reason for the wait.
deepSteps.prose: Thirty seconds feels long standing there. It is the number B&T publishes and it is not negotiable.
deepSteps.quote:
8.	 If a cartridge fails to ignite, keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction and open the chamber only 
after a minimum of 30 seconds.
deepSteps.cite: B&T APC9/10/40/45 PRO OPERATOR’S MANUAL (TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US) — TM-APC9_10_40_45 PRO-AA-00-US — 1.2 Maintenance rules, rule 8, p.17

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Cleaning rod of suitable length with a COPPER brush
Barrel cleaned from the REAR side

cleaning.name: RECEIVERS
tasks: Small brush into the cavities of BOTH lower and upper receiver
All accessible surfaces wiped with an oiled rag
Slight film of oil on all accessible STEEL surfaces

cleaning.name: INSPECTION
tasks: All components checked for cracks, deformations and deterioration
Armorer inspection after each mission, minimum once per year

reassembly: Upper receiver assembled first (with or without the suppressor variant).
Bolt in, pushed until aligned with the cutout; bolt securing pin in from either side.
⛔ Recoil spring into the lock CURVED END FIRST — alignment checked.
Stock into the receiver and pushed upwards; telescopic stock EXTENDED.
Lower onto upper; front and rear take-down pins pushed in from the RIGHT.
Functional check executed before anything is loaded.
fncheck: B&T's own functional check, on a cleared weapon: press the RIGHT-side bolt catch — the bolt shall snap closed. Pull the charging handle fully back and push the bolt catch upward — the bolt shall stay open. Press the LEFT-side bolt catch — it shall snap closed. Engage the safety and pull the trigger — the hammer shall NOT strike. Rotate the right-side fire selector to single fire and back to safe — it shall snap audibly in both positions. In single fire, pull the trigger and hold — the hammer shall strike audibly; cycle the charging handle, release the trigger and pull again — it shall strike again. ⚠ B&T's list continues to a FULL AUTO position because this book also covers select-fire variants; that step is in the document and it is not this firearm's.
